generalQuestions.text: In Germany, people may openly say things against the government because …
answers: people have the right to vote.
generalQuestions.explanation: Freedom of expression is enshrined as a fundamental right in the Basic Law.

generalQuestions.text: In Germany, until a child’s 14th birthday, parents may decide whether the child participates in …
generalQuestions.explanation: Participation in religious education up to age 14 is primarily the parents’ decision.

generalQuestions.text: Germany is a state governed by the rule of law. What does that mean?
answers: All residents and the state must comply with the law.
The state does not have to comply with the law.
Only Germans have to obey the law.
generalQuestions.explanation: In a constitutional state, both the state and citizens are bound by law.

generalQuestions.text: Which right is one of the fundamental rights in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Freedom of expression is a fundamental right guaranteed by the Basic Law.

generalQuestions.text: Elections in Germany are free. What does that mean?
answers: One may accept money in return for voting for a particular candidate.
Only people who have never been in prison may vote.
Voters must not be influenced or forced to vote in a particular way and may not suffer disadvantages because of their vote.
generalQuestions.explanation: Freedom of the vote means a decision without coercion or undue influence.

generalQuestions.text: What is the name of the German constitution?
generalQuestions.explanation: The constitution of Germany is called the Basic Law (Grundgesetz).

generalQuestions.text: Which right is guaranteed as a fundamental right by the German constitution? The right to …
generalQuestions.explanation: Freedom of faith and conscience is protected by the Basic Law.

generalQuestions.text: What is NOT stated in Germany’s Basic Law?
answers: Everyone should have the same amount of money.
All are equal before the law.
generalQuestions.explanation: Equal income is not a constitutional principle.

generalQuestions.text: Which fundamental right applies in Germany only to foreigners? The fundamental right to …
generalQuestions.explanation: The fundamental right to asylum is expressly aimed at those persecuted on political grounds from abroad.

generalQuestions.text: What is compatible with Germany’s Basic Law?
generalQuestions.explanation: Corporal punishment, torture and the death penalty are prohibited; a monetary fine is permissible.

generalQuestions.text: What is the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany called?
generalQuestions.explanation: The official name of the constitution is the Basic Law.

generalQuestions.text: A party in the German Bundestag wants to abolish freedom of the press. Is that possible?
answers: Yes, if more than half of the members of parliament agree.
Yes, but it would require two thirds of members of parliament to agree.
No, because freedom of the press is a fundamental right. It cannot be abolished.
No, because only the Bundesrat can abolish freedom of the press.
generalQuestions.explanation: As a fundamental right, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected.

generalQuestions.text: In parliament, the term "opposition" stands for …
answers: the parliamentary group with the most seats.
all parties that surpassed the 5% threshold in the last election.
all members of parliament who do not belong to the governing party/parties.
generalQuestions.explanation: The opposition consists of all parties that are not part of the government.

generalQuestions.text: Freedom of expression in Germany means that I …
answers: may insult passers-by on the street.
can express my opinion on the internet.
may publicly wear Nazi, Hamas or Islamic State symbols.
may express my opinion only as long as I don’t contradict the government.
generalQuestions.explanation: Expression of opinion is protected, but insults and anti-constitutional symbols are prohibited.

generalQuestions.text: What does Germany’s Basic Law prohibit?
generalQuestions.explanation: Forced labor is constitutionally prohibited.

generalQuestions.text: When is freedom of expression restricted in Germany?
answers: in the public dissemination of false statements about individuals
when expressing opinions about the federal government
generalQuestions.explanation: Untrue, reputation-damaging statements of fact are not protected.

generalQuestions.text: German laws prohibit …
answers: unequal treatment of citizens by the state.
generalQuestions.explanation: The state may not treat anyone unequally without objective justification.

generalQuestions.text: Which fundamental right is guaranteed in Article 1 of the Basic Law of the Federal Republic of Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Article 1 of the Basic Law places human dignity under special protection.

generalQuestions.text: What is meant by the right of "freedom of movement" in Germany?
answers: One may choose one’s place of residence freely.
One may choose a different religion.
One may move about in public only lightly clothed.
generalQuestions.explanation: Freedom of movement means the free choice of place of stay and residence.

generalQuestions.text: A party in Germany pursues the goal of establishing a dictatorship. It is then …
answers: oriented toward the rule of law.
generalQuestions.explanation: Goals directed against the free democratic basic order are unconstitutional.

generalQuestions.text: Which is the coat of arms of the Federal Republic of Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The coat of arms of the Federal Republic of Germany shows a black eagle on a golden background.

generalQuestions.text: What form of government does Germany have?
generalQuestions.explanation: Germany is a parliamentary republic.

generalQuestions.text: In Germany, most working people are …
answers: employed by a company or public authority.
generalQuestions.explanation: The majority work as employees in companies or public authorities.

generalQuestions.text: How many federal states does the Federal Republic of Germany have?
generalQuestions.explanation: Germany consists of 16 federal states.

generalQuestions.text: Which is not a federal state of the Federal Republic of Germany?

generalQuestions.text: Germany is …
answers: a democratic and social federal state.
a social and socialist federal state.
generalQuestions.explanation: The Basic Law defines Germany as a democratic and social federal state.

generalQuestions.text: Germany is …
generalQuestions.explanation: Powers are divided between the federation and the states.

generalQuestions.text: Who elects the members of the Bundestag in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Citizens elect the members of the Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: Which animal is the heraldic animal of the Federal Republic of Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The heraldic animal of the Federal Republic of Germany is the eagle.

generalQuestions.text: Which is not a characteristic of our democracy?
generalQuestions.explanation: Censorship contradicts democratic basic principles.

generalQuestions.text: The cooperation of parties to form a government is called in Germany …
generalQuestions.explanation: Coalitions arise when no party can govern alone and several parties work together.

generalQuestions.text: Which is not a branch of state power in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The three powers are legislative, executive and judicial. The media are not a state power, though sometimes referred to as the fourth estate.

generalQuestions.text: Which statement is correct? In Germany …
answers: state and religious communities are separated.
the state is dependent on religious communities.
state and religious communities form a unity.
generalQuestions.explanation: Germany is a religiously neutral state with separation of state and religion.

generalQuestions.text: What is Germany not?
answers: a state governed by the rule of law

generalQuestions.text: With what does the German state finance social insurance?
generalQuestions.explanation: Social insurance is financed by contributions from employees and employers.

generalQuestions.text: Which measure creates social security in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Statutory health insurance is part of social security.

generalQuestions.text: What are the heads of government of most federal states in Germany called?
generalQuestions.explanation: In almost all Länder, the official title is Minister-President.

generalQuestions.text: The Federal Republic of Germany is a democratic and social …
generalQuestions.explanation: Germany is a federal state with Länder and federation.

generalQuestions.text: What does every German federal state have?
generalQuestions.explanation: Each state has its own state government.

generalQuestions.text: With which words does the German national anthem begin?
answers: Joy, beautiful spark of the gods …

generalQuestions.text: Why are there more than one party in a democracy?
answers: because this represents the differing opinions of citizens
generalQuestions.explanation: Multi-party systems reflect the diversity of interests and opinions.

generalQuestions.text: Who passes a new law in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Laws are passed by parliaments.

generalQuestions.text: When can a party be banned in Germany?
answers: when its campaign is too expensive
when it fights against the constitution
when it criticizes the head of state
when its program proposes a new direction

generalQuestions.text: Whom can citizens in Germany not elect directly?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal President is elected by the Federal Convention, not directly by the people.

generalQuestions.text: To which insurance does long-term care insurance belong?
generalQuestions.explanation: Long-term care insurance is part of the statutory social insurance in Germany.

generalQuestions.text: The German state has many tasks. Which task belongs to them?
answers: It provides all residents free of charge with newspapers.
generalQuestions.explanation: The state provides public infrastructure such as roads and educational institutions.

generalQuestions.text: The German state has many tasks. Which task does not belong to them?
answers: It pays for holidays for all citizens.
generalQuestions.explanation: Paying for holidays is not among the tasks of the state.

generalQuestions.text: Which body is not one of Germany’s constitutional organs?
generalQuestions.explanation: The citizens’ assembly is not a constitutional organ. The constitutional organs are the Bundestag, Bundesrat, Federal Government, Federal President and Federal Constitutional Court.

generalQuestions.text: Who determines education policy in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Education is the responsibility of the states in Germany. Therefore the federal states decide on education policy.

generalQuestions.text: The economic system in Germany is called …
generalQuestions.explanation: The social market economy combines free markets and capitalism with social balancing by the state.

generalQuestions.text: Which does not belong to a democratic state governed by the rule of law?
answers: People can express criticism of the government.
People are arrested by a private police without cause.
Someone commits a crime and is arrested for it.
generalQuestions.explanation: In a state governed by the rule of law, no one may be arbitrarily arrested by a private police force.

generalQuestions.text: What does 'popular sovereignty' mean? All state authority emanates from the …
generalQuestions.explanation: Article 20 of the Basic Law: 'All state authority emanates from the people.'

generalQuestions.text: What does 'constitutional state' (Rechtsstaat) mean in Germany?
answers: The state must comply with the law.
generalQuestions.explanation: A constitutional state means that the state too is bound by law.

generalQuestions.text: Which is not a state power in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: 'Directive' is not a branch of state power in Germany.

the Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe

generalQuestions.text: Which office in Germany is part of the municipal administration?
generalQuestions.explanation: The public order office is part of the municipal administration.

generalQuestions.text: Who is usually elected President of the German Bundestag?
answers: the minister-president of the largest federal state
a member of the strongest parliamentary group
generalQuestions.explanation: Usually the election is from the strongest parliamentary group.

generalQuestions.text: Who appoints the ministers of the Federal Government in Germany?
answers: the president of the Federal Constitutional Court
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal President appoints the federal ministers.

generalQuestions.text: About how many years ago was there first a Jewish community in the territory of present-day Germany?

generalQuestions.text: In Germany, the Bundestag and Bundesrat belong to the …
generalQuestions.explanation: Bundestag and Bundesrat are federal legislative bodies (legislature).

generalQuestions.text: What does 'popular sovereignty' mean?
answers: The queen/king rules over the people.
The Federal Constitutional Court stands above the constitution.
Interest groups exercise sovereignty together with the government.
State authority emanates from the people.
generalQuestions.explanation: The people are the bearer of sovereignty, meaning all state authority emanates from the people.

generalQuestions.text: When the parliament of a German federal state is elected, it is called …
generalQuestions.explanation: Elections at the state level are called state parliament elections (Landtagswahlen).

generalQuestions.text: What does not belong to the executive branch in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Courts are part of the judiciary, not the executive.

generalQuestions.text: Today, the Federal Republic of Germany is structured into …
answers: an eastern state and a western state.
generalQuestions.explanation: The federal structure consists of federation, states (Länder) and municipalities.

generalQuestions.text: It is not among the tasks of the German Bundestag to …
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal Cabinet is not formed by the Bundestag. It consists of the Federal Chancellor and the federal ministers.

generalQuestions.text: Which cities have the largest Jewish communities in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The largest communities today are traditionally in Berlin and Munich.

generalQuestions.text: What is primarily a task of the federal states in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Education is the responsibility of the states; this includes education policy.

generalQuestions.text: Why does the state in Germany oversee the school system?
answers: because there are only public schools in Germany
because all students must have a school-leaving certificate
because there are different schools in the federal states
because it is its task according to the Basic Law
generalQuestions.explanation: The state has supervision over the school system according to the constitution.

generalQuestions.text: The Federal Republic of Germany has a three-tier administrative structure. What is the lowest political level called?
generalQuestions.explanation: The lowest level is the municipalities (local communities).

generalQuestions.text: In 1974, Federal President Gustav Heinemann presented Helmut Schmidt with the appointment certificate as Federal Chancellor. Which is one of the tasks of the Federal President?
answers: He/She proposes the Chancellor for election.

generalQuestions.text: Where does the German Federal Chancellor most often stay?
answers: in Bonn, because the Federal Chancellery and the Bundestag are there.
at Schloss Meseberg, the federal government’s guest house, to receive state guests.
at Schloss Bellevue, the official residence of the Federal President, to receive state guests.
in Berlin, because the Federal Chancellery and the Bundestag are there.

generalQuestions.text: What is the name of the current Federal Chancellor of Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The current Federal Chancellor is Friedrich Merz.

generalQuestions.text: The two largest parliamentary groups in the German Bundestag are currently …
generalQuestions.explanation: The two largest groups are CDU/CSU and AfD.

generalQuestions.text: What is the name of the parliament for all of Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The all-German parliament is the German Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: What is the name of Germany’s current head of state?
generalQuestions.explanation: The head of state is the Federal President; currently Frank-Walter Steinmeier.

generalQuestions.text: What does the abbreviation CDU stand for in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: CDU stands for Christian Democratic Union.

generalQuestions.text: What is the Bundeswehr?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Bundeswehr is the armed force of the Federal Republic.

generalQuestions.text: What does the abbreviation SPD stand for?
generalQuestions.explanation: SPD stands for Social Democratic Party of Germany.

generalQuestions.text: What does the abbreviation FDP mean in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: FDP stands for Free Democratic Party.

generalQuestions.text: Which court in Germany is responsible for interpreting the Basic Law?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal Constitutional Court guards the constitution.

generalQuestions.text: Who elects the Federal Chancellor in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Chancellor is elected by the German Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: Who leads the German Federal Cabinet?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal Cabinet is led by the Chancellor.

generalQuestions.text: Who elects the German Federal Chancellor?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Chancellor is elected by the Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: What is the main task of the Federal President of Germany?
answers: He/She monitors compliance with the laws.
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal President is the head of state and represents the Federal Republic of Germany externally.

generalQuestions.text: Who forms the German Bundesrat?
answers: the ministers of the Federal Government
the government representatives of the federal states
generalQuestions.explanation: In the Bundesrat, the governments of the states represent their interests.

generalQuestions.text: Who elects the Federal President in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Federal Convention consists of members of the Bundestag and representatives of the state parliaments.

generalQuestions.text: Who is the head of state of the Federal Republic of Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: The head of state is the Federal President.

generalQuestions.text: The parliamentary opposition in the German Bundestag …
answers: decides who becomes a federal minister.
determines who sits in the Bundesrat.
proposes the heads of government of the states.
generalQuestions.explanation: The opposition has the important task of scrutinizing the government.

generalQuestions.text: What is the association of members of a party in parliament called in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Members of the same party form a parliamentary group (Fraktion) to pursue political goals together.

generalQuestions.text: The German federal states participate in federal legislation through …
generalQuestions.explanation: The Bundesrat represents the states and participates in federal legislation.

generalQuestions.text: In Germany, a change of government in a federal state can affect federal politics. Governing becomes …
answers: more difficult if it changes the majority in the Bundestag.
easier if new parties enter the Bundesrat as a result.
more difficult if it changes the majority in the Bundesrat.
easier if it is a rich federal state.
generalQuestions.explanation: If the majority balance in the Bundesrat changes, it can influence federal politics.

generalQuestions.text: What does the abbreviation CSU mean in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: CSU stands for Christian Social Union – it is the sister party of the CDU in Bavaria.

generalQuestions.text: The more 'second votes' a party receives in a federal election, the …
answers: fewer first votes it can have.
more of the party's direct candidates enter parliament.
greater the risk of having to form a coalition.
more seats the party receives in parliament.
generalQuestions.explanation: The second vote determines the distribution of seats among parties in the Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: From what age may one participate in the election to the German Bundestag?
generalQuestions.explanation: The active right to vote for the Bundestag is enshrined in the Basic Law and applies from age 18.

generalQuestions.text: What applies to most children in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Germany has general compulsory schooling.

generalQuestions.text: How can someone who denies the Holocaust be punished?
answers: up to 100 hours of community service
not at all; Holocaust denial is allowed
imprisonment of up to five years or a fine

generalQuestions.text: What do you automatically pay in Germany if you are permanently employed?
generalQuestions.explanation: Employees automatically pay contributions to social insurance.

generalQuestions.text: If members of the German Bundestag change their parliamentary group, …
answers: they are no longer allowed to attend meetings.
the government may lose its majority.
generalQuestions.explanation: Changing parliamentary groups can change the majority relationships in the Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: Who pays for social insurance in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Social insurance is jointly financed by employers and employees.

generalQuestions.text: Which does not belong to the statutory social insurance?
generalQuestions.explanation: Life insurance is private and not legally required.

generalQuestions.text: Trade unions are interest groups of ...
generalQuestions.explanation: Trade unions represent the interests of employees.

generalQuestions.text: With what can one be honored in the Federal Republic of Germany for outstanding achievements in politics, business, culture, science or social affairs? With the ...
answers: Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany
honorary title "Hero of the German Democratic Republic"
generalQuestions.explanation: In the Federal Republic of Germany, the highest award for special merits is the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany.

generalQuestions.text: What is referred to in Germany as a 'traffic light coalition'? The cooperation ...
answers: of the CDU and CSU parliamentary groups in the Bundestag
of the SPD, FDP and Alliance 90/The Greens in a government
of the CSU, The Left and Alliance 90/The Greens in a government

generalQuestions.text: What is a task of election workers in Germany?

generalQuestions.text: For how many years is the German Bundestag elected?
generalQuestions.explanation: The legislative period of the German Bundestag is usually four years (Art. 39 Basic Law).

generalQuestions.text: In a Bundestag election in Germany, anyone may vote who ...
answers: lives in the Federal Republic of Germany and wants to vote.
is a citizen of the Federal Republic of Germany and at least 18 years old.

generalQuestions.explanation: German citizens aged 18 and over have the active right to vote in Bundestag elections.

generalQuestions.text: How often are Bundestag elections normally held in Germany?
generalQuestions.explanation: Regularly every four years; exceptions possible if the Bundestag is dissolved.

generalQuestions.text: For how many years is the Bundestag in Germany elected?
generalQuestions.explanation: Here, too, the correct answer is: four years (Art. 39 Basic Law).

generalQuestions.text: Which actions relating to the State of Israel are prohibited in Germany?
answers: hanging an Israeli flag on private property
the public call for the annihilation of Israel
generalQuestions.explanation: Calling for genocide is a criminal offense (e.g., incitement to hatred).

generalQuestions.text: Elections in Germany are ...
generalQuestions.explanation: Elections must, among other things, be secret (Art. 38 Basic Law).

generalQuestions.text: In Germany, the election is won by the party that ...
answers: was mostly chosen by the majority of men.
received the most votes from manual workers.
received the most first votes for its candidate for Chancellor.
generalQuestions.explanation: What is decisive is the majority of votes cast.

generalQuestions.text: Taking part in democratic elections in Germany is ...
generalQuestions.explanation: There is a right to vote, but no compulsory voting.

generalQuestions.text: What does 'active right to vote' mean in Germany?
answers: You must help count the votes.
generalQuestions.explanation: Active suffrage means the right to cast one’s vote.

generalQuestions.explanation: Being allowed to vote refers to the active right to vote.

generalQuestions.explanation: The threshold clause is 5% of second votes. Below that, a party receives no seats in the Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: Who is allowed to become a member of the approximately 40 Jewish Maccabi sports clubs?
generalQuestions.explanation: The Maccabi clubs are open to everyone.

generalQuestions.text: Elections in Germany are free. What does that mean?
answers: All convicted criminals are not allowed to vote.
If I want to vote, my employer must give me time off.
Each person can decide without coercion whether they want to vote and whom they want to vote for.
I can freely decide where I want to go to vote.
generalQuestions.explanation: Free means voting without coercion and undue influence.

generalQuestions.text: The electoral system in Germany is a ...
answers: combination of majority and proportional representation.
generalQuestions.explanation: Personalized proportional representation: a combination of majority and proportional representation.

generalQuestions.text: A party wants to enter the German Bundestag. However, it must have a minimum share of votes. This is called ...
generalQuestions.explanation: The 5% threshold limits the entry of very small parties.

generalQuestions.text: What principle do elections in Germany follow? Elections in Germany are ...
generalQuestions.explanation: Principle of free, equal and secret elections (Art. 38 Basic Law).

generalQuestions.text: What is the '5% threshold' in Germany?
answers: a voting rule in the Bundestag for small parties
attendance control in the Bundestag for votes
minimum share of votes required to enter parliament
attendance control in the Bundesrat for votes
generalQuestions.explanation: Parties need at least 5% of second votes for seats in the Bundestag.

generalQuestions.text: The Bundestag election in Germany is the election of ...
generalQuestions.explanation: In the Bundestag election, the all-German parliament is elected.

generalQuestions.text: In a democracy, one function of regular elections is to ...
answers: force citizens to cast their vote.
enable a change of government according to the will of the majority of voters.
maintain the existing laws in the country.
give more power to the poor.
generalQuestions.explanation: Elections enable a peaceful change of government according to the will of the majority.

generalQuestions.text: What do eligible voters in Germany receive before an election?
answers: an election notification from the municipality
a voting permit from the Federal President
a notification from the Federal Convention
a notification from the parish office

because many small parties make it difficult to form a government.

generalQuestions.text: Which ballot paper would be valid in a Bundestag election?

generalQuestions.text: What is permitted in Bundestag and state elections in Germany?
answers: The husband votes on behalf of his wife.

Children from the age of 14 are allowed to vote.

Join a sports club and train cycling.

generalQuestions.text: Which court in Germany is responsible for conflicts in the world of work?

generalQuestions.text: Who advises people on legal matters in Germany and represents them in court?
answers: a female lay judge/a male lay judge

generalQuestions.explanation: Lawyers advise and represent clients.

generalQuestions.text: What is the main task of a judge in Germany? A judge ...
answers: works at a court and delivers judgments.
generalQuestions.explanation: Judges administer justice (judgments, decisions) on the basis of the laws.

generalQuestions.explanation: The judicial power is the judiciary (alongside legislature and executive).

generalQuestions.text: In Germany, a judge belongs to the ...
generalQuestions.explanation: Judges exercise the judicial power (judiciary).

generalQuestions.text: State power is divided in Germany. For which branch of state power does a judge work?
